IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Senate Transportation (originally sponsored by Senators Haugen, Swecker, Sheldon, Hobbs, and White)

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to electric vehicle license fees; adding a newsection to chapter 46.17 RCW; creating new sections; and providing acontingent expiration date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature recognizes that the motorvehicle fuel tax is the primary source of funding for the state'stransportation system. As the state's fleet changes from motorvehicles powered by traditional sources, such as gasoline and diesel,to those powered by electricity, the ability of the state to fund themaintenance and preservation of the transportation system iscompromised. In order to mitigate the impacts of the diminishing motorvehicle fuel tax, and to create a system where each driver pays for afair portion of his or her use of the road, an additional fee isimposed on electric vehicles.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 46.17 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Before accepting an application for a vehicle registration foran electric vehicle that uses propulsion units powered solely by p. 1 SSB 5251electricity, the department, county auditor or other agent, or subagentappointed by the director must require the applicant to pay a onehundred dollar fee in addition to any other fees and taxes required bylaw. The one hundred dollar fee is due at the time of initial vehicleregistration and annual registration renewal. (2) This section only applies to: (a) A vehicle that is designed to have the capability to drive ata speed of more than thirty-five miles per hour; and (b) A vehicle registration that is due on or after March 1, 2012. (3)(a) The fee under this section is imposed to provide funds tomitigate the impact of vehicles on state roads and highways, and isseparate and distinct from other vehicle license fees. Proceeds fromthe fee must be used for highway purposes, and must be deposited in themotor vehicle fund created in RCW 46.68.070, subject to (b) of thissubsection. (b) If in any year the amount of proceeds from the fee collectedunder this section exceeds one million dollars, the excess amount overone million dollars must be deposited as follows: (i) Seventy percent to the motor vehicle fund created in RCW46.68.070; (ii) Fifteen percent to the transportation improvement accountcreated in RCW 47.26.084; and (iii) Fifteen percent to the rural arterial trust account createdin RCW 36.79.020.
Section 2 of this act expires on theeffective date of legislation enacted by the legislature that imposesa vehicle miles traveled fee or tax.

The department of transportation mustprovide written notice of the expiration date of section 2 of this actto affected parties, the chief clerk of the house of representatives,the secretary of the senate, the office of the code reviser, and othersas deemed appropriate by the department.
